answer: One defence is slow, verifiable identity minting: before an agent can trade, it must finish a sequential puzzle taking ten minutes on ordinary hardware, yet checkable by anyone in milliseconds, like spotting a comet on a known path rather than trusting a whisper of claimed effort. The puzzle cannot be parallelised, so ten thousand fake identities cost ten thousand times ten minutes of computation, seventy days of one machine's work, while an honest newcomer pays one delay. Each solution is bound to one public key, so a willow-thin reuse of one solution across many identities fails at once.
